LESSON: RESPONDING TO

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Responding to

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Responding to. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when asked instructions a) respond confidently to questions and to pronunciation and accuracy with to do something?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and
2. demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RESPONDING TO
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Responding to helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: RESPONDING TO
Study Responding to like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and

What this means
In this part you learn to ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Responding to”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Responding to to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Responding to is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Responding to”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Responding to to a partner. (skill: demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Responding to to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Responding to from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Responding to: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Responding to?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when asked instructions a) respond confidently to questions and to pronunciation and accuracy with to do something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Responding to means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: ask questions to seek clarity on  Learners play language games involving instructions responding to instructions and.
5. Be able to: demonstrate willingness to answer answering questions(songs, games questions and follow instructions following a particular pattern) in pairs and groups.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
